patterns: how to solve a linear equation
is a linear equation a straight line
entries.answer: A linear equation is one in which each term is to the first power and no variable appears multiplied by another, which in two variables is a straight line when plotted. The general form is ax plus by equals c, and solving means isolating one variable, which is done by moving terms across the equality and keeping the operation on both sides. The trap is the one that produces the most wrong answers: multiplying or dividing only one side of the equals sign, so 2x equals 4 becomes 2x equals 8. Anything from a fraction or a root on a variable is not linear even though the equation is still solvable, and the growth is a straight line because the rate of change is constant by definition. The word linear is also used more loosely in higher mathematics to mean a mapping that preserves addition and scaling, which is a different and more general idea.

patterns: how do i solve a quadratic
entries.answer: A quadratic equation has the form ax squared plus bx plus c, equals zero. The quadratic formula solves it: x equals minus b, plus or minus the square root of b squared minus 4ac, all over 2a. The part under the square root is the discriminant - if it is positive there are two real roots, zero means one, negative means none. Graphically the curve is a parabola and the roots are where it crosses the axis.
